label: F1RL passive 1-link LC fibre TAP
description: Passive 1-link optical TAP for a duplex LC fibre run: the two network LC ports stay mated to the live link and each direction is split onto its own monitor LC port, at a 50/50 (or 60/40, 70/30, 80/20) ratio. Unpowered, no IP stack, no management - a dead TAP cannot drop the link it sits in.
notes: Profitap LC TAP datasheet (v4.3): '1 network link / 1 monitor link', LC connectors with zirconia sleeve adapters, passive and unpowered. The vendor sells the same passive hardware across a rate ladder - MM 62.5 um to 1 Gbps, OM4 to 1-100 Gbps, SM 9 um to 1-400 Gbps - and split ratios 50/50, 60/40, 70/30, 80/20 (part suffix -50/-60/-70/-80). Modelled here as the 1G/10G LC class the catalogue's fibre ports run at; the split ratio is not a modelling knob, because the simulator carries the copy at line rate either way. Insertion loss (50/50, MM 50 um): 3.8 dB per direction. The hardware presents LC/UPC adapters, not cages; the four ports are modelled as SFP+ because a link in this simulator runs port to port and both ends must be the same cage class for a cable to exist at all - the convention the Garland fibre taps already set. Cabling it to an LC/UPC port instead is refused by the engine, which is the one thing a passive tap must never do to a lab.
